units: Metric document defines telemetry intended to measure causal authority of empirical consequences over future mechanism behavior.
Measurement chain is E* -> Phi_R(e_t) -> Delta W -> W_(t+1).
LBR=N_inadmissible/N_total and is framed as empirical friction rather than causal attribution.
High LBR alone is explicitly insufficient to justify an update; residuals must be attributed first.
C_post is post-error confidence in an updated explanation and is bounded in [0,1].
Confidence change does not imply authority change.
MRAT outputs simplex attribution vector over noise, state, mechanism, representation, and generator.
Desired behavior inserts attribution between residual and authority update rather than direct error-triggered update.
Possible distance implementations include syntax-tree, execution-graph, causal-graph, or representation-topology distance.
Authority half-life is earliest t with invalid authority <= half initial authority.
ADI conceptually measures divergence between observed contradiction and actual mechanism revision.
Document leaves ADI as generic f(LBR,C_post,R_update), not a unique closed-form equation.
Full RAHU profile is (LBR,Phi_R,R_update,ARR,tau_authority,ACS), not only a single scalar.
Source predicts qualitative healthy, noise-reactive, and decoupled metric signatures.
Metric dependency graph places LBR before MRAT, structural branch before authority update, ARR before ACS.
Constraint choice and trajectory sampling determine LBR but are not identified as universal.
Post-error confidence is system-dependent and lacks a cross-system calibration procedure.
Attribution vector construct validity is not established.
No canonical D or theta is selected or validated.
Authority proxy validity is not established.
Document's ADI is conceptual f(...) and therefore underdetermined until an implementation is selected.
ACS validity inherits uncertainty from ADI, ARR, and tau_adapt.
Qualitative signatures are predictions, not reported observations.
